research_questions: CANDIDATE SCOPE: the surveyed set is DBML, Mermaid erDiagram (incumbent baseline), LinkML, PlantUML IE/Chen notation, Prisma schema language, Atlas HCL (ariga.io), and D2 with SQL table shapes. tbls, SchemaSpy, and ERAlchemy2 were dropped from the seed list at planning time, all for the same reason: each is a reverse-engineering documentation generator whose authoritative source is a live database connection, a JDBC introspection target, or SQLAlchemy runtime metadata, not a plain-text, human-authored, version-controlled model. This inverts the direction the brief requires (the specification artifact must be authoritative), the same exclusion the brief already applies to code-first ORMs. If source-gathering later finds a plain-text, spec-first authoring mode for any of the three (e.g. tbls consuming a hand-written schema file rather than a live DB), the assignee for that candidate must record it as new evidence and the drop must be revisited, not silently upheld.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express a composite primary key spanning two non-surrogate columns, as OUTCOME_RULE needs on (task_version_id, sequence_no), NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK needs on (task_version_id, resource_name), and CONDITION_POST needs on (condition_id, date_key)? Answer expressible / expressible-only-via-workaround / not-expressible, citing the exact grammar rule or documentation section.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express an opaque JSON payload column, as TASK_VERSION needs for schedule_spec, window_spec, dependency_spec, output_condition_spec, retry_spec, and cyclic_spec? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express an enumerated string domain constrained to a fixed value set, as FOLDER_RUN.execution_context needs (SCHEDULED or MANUAL) and NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.link_kind needs (HOST_CAPACITY or NAMED_RESOURCE)? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express several distinct self-referencing foreign keys on one table, as TASK_INSTANCE needs for origin_instance_id, cyclic_root_instance_id, and previous_iteration_id simultaneously? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.
For each surveyed candidate: can it express a nullable foreign key, as TASK_INSTANCE.folder_run_id and TASK_INSTANCE.plan_id both need? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express a multi-column UNIQUE constraint not tied to the primary key, as PLAN needs on (domain_id, odate) and NAMED_RESOURCE needs on (domain_id, name)? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.
For each surveyed candidate: can it express a one-to-zero-or-one relationship, as ATTEMPT ||--o| ATTEMPT_RESULT needs? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express a value constraint beyond type, as NAMED_RESOURCE_LINK.resource_task_weight needs (a decimal positive integer OR the literal ALL)? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: can it express several logical schemas inside one database, matching the configuration, runtime, audit, and resources split described in docs/adr/0001-single-database-domain-scoping.md and docs/arc42/00-system-map.md line 121? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation.

For each surveyed candidate: does its validator (or an available lint/generation step) support asserting a cross-cutting convention such as domain_id present on every Domain-owned table? Answer with the same three-way classification and citation, distinguishing a built-in rule from a workaround (e.g. a custom lint script layered on top).

For each surveyed candidate: does a validator exist, and does it exit non-zero on a malformed or internally inconsistent model, so the artifact could sit behind a deterministic CI gate the way factory/scripts/structurizr's validate subcommand does for architecture? Cite the exact command and observed (or documented) exit-code contract.

For each surveyed candidate: is a Docker image published, and under what exact image name and tag, verified against the public registry listing (Docker Hub or ghcr.io tag list) rather than a README or blog claim? Record the registry URL consulted and the tag observed.
For each surveyed candidate: does the toolchain export SVG from inside that Docker image with no local install, matching factory/scripts/structurizr's export-svg subcommand?
For each surveyed candidate: does the toolchain export PNG from inside that Docker image with no local install, matching factory/scripts/structurizr's export-png subcommand?

For each surveyed candidate: does it support named subset views over one model, so a 25-entity model can be split into readable sub-diagrams the way Structurizr's views do for architecture? Cite the exact mechanism, or record its absence.

For each surveyed candidate: can it generate application-level types (Pydantic models, SQLAlchemy mappings, dataclasses, or equivalent), and if so, do the advanced constructs above (composite PKs, JSON columns, enums, multiple self-referencing FKs, nullable FKs, multi-column UNIQUE, one-to-zero-or-one, the ALL-or-integer value constraint) survive that generation intact or degrade/drop? Record per-construct survival, not just yes/no for generation existing.

For each surveyed candidate that generates application types: can physical DDL also be derived from the same source artifact, and does that DDL preserve the advanced constructs? If no type generation exists, record DDL derivation as not applicable rather than not expressible.

For each surveyed candidate: what is its licence (exact SPDX identifier or licence name and version), and what is its governance model (single-vendor, foundation-governed, BDFL, community/consensus), sourced from the repository's LICENSE file and governance or CONTRIBUTING documentation?

For each surveyed candidate: what is the date of the most recent tagged release and the date of the most recent repository activity (commit, merge, or release), and does either fall within the 18 months before August 2026 (i.e. since roughly February 2025)? Flag any candidate failing both as at risk of abandonment per the brief's freshness_requirements.

For each surveyed candidate: what does a documented contrary-evidence search turn up — open issues describing missing features among the advanced constructs above, a documented limitations page, or explicit 'not supported' statements in official docs? Record search terms, where searched, and the result even when nothing was found.
search_angles: Official grammar or language specification published by the candidate's maintaining org or project (e.g. a formal grammar file, an EBNF definition, or a 'language reference' documentation page) — the primary source for every expressible/not-expressible citation.

Official documentation site (docs.<project>.io, readthedocs, or the project's own docs/ directory rendered as a site) for validator behaviour, view/subset support, generation targets, and DDL derivation.
The project's own GitHub (or equivalent) repository: README, docs/ folder, CONTRIBUTING.md or GOVERNANCE.md, LICENSE file.
The project's release tags page (GitHub Releases or equivalent) for version history and the most recent release date.

The project's issue tracker, searched for open issues naming the advanced constructs (composite key, JSON column, enum, self-referencing FK, nullable FK, multi-column unique, one-to-zero-or-one, custom value constraint, multiple schemas, cross-cutting column lint) to find both confirmations and known gaps.
The public container registry tag listing (hub.docker.com/r/<image> or ghcr.io/<org>/<image>/tags) for image availability and exact tags — never a README or blog claim standing in for this check.
The repository's LICENSE file directly, for the licence source_targets item, rather than a third-party licence-summary site.
Governance or maintainer documentation (GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, an 'About' or 'Team' page, or a foundation charter if the project sits under one such as a Linux Foundation or similar body).

CONTRARY-EVIDENCE ANGLE (mandatory per the evidence policy's contrary-evidence-search requirement): search the project's issue tracker and docs for limitations pages, 'known issues', 'not supported', or 'unsupported' statements touching the advanced constructs, validator exit-code behaviour, Docker packaging, view/subset support, or generation fidelity. Record the search even when it finds nothing.
source_targets: PRIMARY: the official language grammar or specification document maintained by the candidate's own project or org — required for every 'expressible' citation.
PRIMARY: the official documentation site or in-repo docs/ maintained by the candidate's own project — required for validator, view, generation, and DDL-derivation claims.
PRIMARY: the candidate's own source-code repository, including its release tags list and issue tracker.

PRIMARY: the public container registry's own tag-listing page (Docker Hub or ghcr.io) — required for any Docker-availability claim; a blog post or README asserting 'available on Docker Hub' is not sufficient on its own.
PRIMARY: the repository's LICENSE file, read directly, for the licence field.

PRIMARY: the repository's governance/maintainer documentation (GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md) or, absent that, the visible maintainer/organisation structure on the repository itself, for the governance field.

SECONDARY (leads only, never sole evidence for a capability claim): comparison articles, blog posts, and community write-ups comparing data-modeling DSLs — useful for discovering constructs or gaps to check against a primary source, never cited as the sole support for an 'expressible' or 'not expressible' answer.
assignments: Candidate: DBML (@dbml/cli, dbml-renderer, and the dbdiagram.io DBML language). Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to DBML — the DBML language reference grammar, dbdiagram.io/@dbml/cli docs, the dbml GitHub repo (releases, issues), Docker registry listing for any dbml-cli or dbml-renderer image, licence file, governance, and last-activity date — plus the mandatory contrary-evidence search for each advanced construct. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-dbml-*.json (one file per facet, e.g. source-dbml-grammar.json, source-dbml-docker.json, source-dbml-generation.json, source-dbml-licence-governance.json, source-dbml-contrary-evidence.json); no other assignment may write a file under this prefix.

Candidate: Mermaid erDiagram (the incumbent baseline currently embedded in docs/spec/supplementary_specs/entity-model.md). Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to Mermaid's erDiagram syntax — the Mermaid official docs' entity-relationship-diagram syntax reference, the mermaid-js GitHub repo (releases, issues), the mermaid-cli Docker image registry listing, licence file, governance, last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to whether Mermaid's validator (mermaid-cli's exit behaviour on malformed diagrams) and its lack of named subset views over one model are documented facts, not assumptions, since this candidate is the artifact under replacement. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-mermaid-erd-*.json.

Candidate: LinkML. Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to LinkML — the LinkML official specification/metamodel docs, the linkml GitHub repo (releases, issues), the linkml Docker image registry listing (if any) or documented containerised validation path, licence file, governance (LinkML is maintained under a documented steering process), last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to LinkML's YAML-based schema constructs for composite keys, enums, and its documented Pydantic/SQLAlchemy generators and whether the advanced constructs survive that generation. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-linkml-*.json.

Candidate: PlantUML IE/Chen notation (entity-relationship diagrams via PlantUML's IE or Chen-notation support). Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to PlantUML's ER notation — the official PlantUML language reference guide's entity-relationship section, the plantuml GitHub repo (releases, issues), the plantuml Docker image registry listing, licence file, governance, last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to whether PlantUML has any semantic validator beyond syntax parsing (relevant to the exit-code research question) and whether it supports named subset views over one model. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-plantuml-ie-*.json.

Candidate: Prisma schema language. Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to the Prisma schema language — the official Prisma schema reference docs, the prisma GitHub repo (releases, issues), the prisma-engines/CLI Docker image registry listing (if published) or documented `npx prisma` containerisation path, licence file, governance (Prisma is a commercial-backed open-source project — record this explicitly), last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to whether Prisma's schema stays product-neutral given its required `datasource` provider field, and whether `prisma validate`/`prisma format --check` exits non-zero on a malformed model. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-prisma-*.json.

Candidate: Atlas HCL (ariga.io). Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to Atlas's HCL schema language — the official Atlas HCL language documentation, the ariga/atlas GitHub repo (releases, issues), the arigaio/atlas Docker image registry listing, licence file, governance (note if dual-licensed or has a commercial tier), last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to whether an HCL schema can stay product-neutral given Atlas's dialect-specific schema blocks, and whether `atlas schema validate`/`atlas schema lint` exits non-zero on a malformed or inconsistent model. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-atlas-hcl-*.json.

Candidate: D2 with SQL table shapes. Bounded task: gather primary-source evidence for every research_question above as applied to D2's sql_table shape — the official D2 documentation's sql_table shape reference, the terrastruct/d2 GitHub repo (releases, issues), the D2 Docker image registry listing, licence file, governance, last-activity date, and the mandatory contrary-evidence search, with explicit attention to whether D2's sql_table shape carries any real constraint semantics (composite keys, uniqueness, enums, value constraints beyond type) versus being a purely visual/label-based table drawing with no validator or generation capability — record this distinction explicitly rather than inferring capability from the diagram's visual richness. agent: researcher; tier: standard; independent_session: false. Owns and writes exclusively under docs/research/data-modeling-dsl/sources/source-d2-sql-table-*.json.
stop_conditions: Stop gathering for a given candidate once every research_question above has an answer with a citation to an exact documentation section or grammar rule (or a recorded 'no primary source found' outcome) — full per-candidate coverage reached.

Stop gathering for a given source_targets category once the primary source (grammar/spec, official docs, project repository, registry tag listing, LICENSE file, governance doc) has been checked and either yielded an answer or is confirmed to not exist for that candidate — primary source exhausted.

Stop gathering for a candidate once it is ruled out on recorded evidence (e.g. no Docker image on any public registry, no validator with exit-code behaviour, or licence terms that make it unusable) — record the reason and the evidence in that candidate's source-<slug>-*.json files; a candidate is never silently dropped from the survey once assigned.

Stop the overall survey once the brief's completion_criteria are all met: at least four candidates surveyed including DBML and Mermaid erDiagram; each candidate has a source record covering language definition, validator/exit behaviour, Docker SVG/PNG rendering, named subset views, application-type generation, DDL derivation, licence, and project activity; every advanced construct is answered for every candidate with a citation; and any pre-planning or in-research candidate drop is recorded with reason and evidence.

Stop searching a single facet (e.g. Docker availability) once a public-registry-listing citation is obtained or its confirmed absence is recorded — do not keep searching once the primary source for that specific facet has given a definitive answer.
Do not proceed to synthesis, ranking, a Pugh Matrix, or an ADR from this plan or its resulting source records — those are separate, later steps outside this survey's stop boundary.
